index_record.dataset_generation_caption: The figure presents a schematic overview of a real zero-shot training pipeline for fine-tuning a CLIP model using ImageNet21k data and Large Language Model (LLM)-generated descriptions. The global layout is structured within a large rounded rectangular container, divided into two main vertical sections: the left side represents input data from ImageNet21k, and the right side shows the LLM-generated object descriptions. At the top, two blue rectangular boxes labeled 'ImageNet21k' and 'LLM' indicate the sources of input. Below these, four rows correspond to example classes: 'Butternut squash', 'Fighter aircraft', 'Hippodamia convergens', and 'llama'. Each row contains an image from ImageNet21k on the left, the class name in red text in the center, and a descriptive text box on the right generated by the LLM. These descriptions focus solely on visual attributes without mentioning the class names—e.g., 'A vegetable with a thick, cream-colored rind' for butternut squash or 'The animal has a long neck' for llama. A vertical brace on the far right groups these descriptions under the label 'Object descriptoin without names'. Below this section, two inverted trapezoidal encoders are shown: a green one labeled 'Image Encoder' and a yellow one labeled 'Text Encoder'. These feed into a central light-blue rectangular box labeled 'Contrastive loss', indicating the training objective. Curved arrows point from both encoders to the loss function, illustrating the contrastive learning setup. Another vertical brace on the right connects the encoders and loss to the label 'Fine-tune CLIP', signifying the overall goal of the pipeline. The entire diagram emphasizes the method of generating attribute-based descriptions without class labels to enable more robust zero-shot classification.
